correctness.rationale: For each fixed integer r>=2 and N>=2, all admissible summand exponents lie in [1,N-1] and conversely every such assignment is below 2^N. Binary uniqueness gives exactly binomial(s,2) twofold labels and no higher collisions. Hence F=ts-binomial(s,2). Root fractional parts satisfy an interval-count discrepancy O_r(K^(1-1/r)) by summing binomial block errors; the normalized remainder differs from shifted negative fractional roots by O_r(t^(-1/r)), preserving this discrepancy after dyadic segmentation. The two uniform laws and no-constant-second-term claim follow. All 294 finite exact-integer test cases passed; they supplement, not prove, the infinite claim.

value.rationale: Precise size of the sparse set A enters the sieve for 2026 Romanoff-type representation theorems. This new theorem determines exact collisions and a complete, effective second-order fluctuation law for the most natural asymmetric mixed-power specialization (1,r). It identifies the critical change in the secondary-term center at r=2, shows that the order-N error cannot be flattened to any fixed linear coefficient, and gives a uniform error distribution for every r>=2; this supplies mathematically motivated boundary information absent from the published leading asymptotic rather than an arbitrary small computation. No prime-density claim is made.
